text: Then it is my duty to break in that door, said Utterson, taking up the kitchen poker, and Poole brought the axe from the laboratory. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked whether the masked thing was Mister Hyde, Poole answered that it was the same size and had the same quick, light way of moving. <break time="0.8s" /> Utterson admitted that the sight of Hyde had always filled him with a strange, cold horror, which was exactly what Poole now described. <break time="0.8s" /> Two servants were sent around to guard the laboratorys back door, which opened onto a side street, so that the creature could not escape. <break time="0.8s" /> In the dark laboratory the two men waited, and from the cabinet above came the sound of footsteps pacing quietly up and down. <break time="0.8s" /> So it walks all day, sir, whispered Poole, and once I heard it weeping like a woman or a lost soul. <break time="0.8s" /> Jekyll, I demand to see you, cried Utterson loudly, and if you will not let me in, I will enter by force. <break time="0.8s" /> Utterson, said the voice, for Gods sake, have mercy, and the lawyer shouted, That is not Jekylls voice, it is Hydes, Down with the door, Poole. <break time="0.8s" /> Poole swung the axe, and a scream of animal terror rang from the cabinet, the door shaking under each blow until it fell inward at the fifth.
